name: Data Retention Policy
description: A policy governing the retention and management of all customer documents, transaction records, policy documentation, audit files, and both physical and digital records held by the bank.
context: Applies to: All customer documents, All transaction records, All policy/procedure documentation, All audit and compliance files, All physical and digital records

name: Retention of All Customer Documents
description: A mandatory requirement that all customer documents must be retained in accordance with the data retention policy scope.

name: Retention of All Transaction Records
description: A mandatory requirement that all transaction records must be retained in accordance with the data retention policy scope.

name: Retention of All Policy and Procedure Documentation
description: A mandatory requirement that all policy and procedure documentation must be retained in accordance with the data retention policy scope.

name: Retention of All Audit and Compliance Files
description: A mandatory requirement that all audit and compliance files must be retained in accordance with the data retention policy scope.

name: Retention of Physical and Digital Records
description: A mandatory requirement that all physical and digital records must be retained in accordance with the data retention policy scope, covering both formats of record storage.

name: Document Retention and Destruction Policy
description: FirstUK Bank's policy governing the retention and secure destruction of documents. The policy establishes that documents are retained only as long as legally required or business-justified, after which they must be destroyed securely. This policy addresses compliance obligations and operational risk management related to document lifecycle management.
context: FirstUK Bank retains documents only as long as legally required or business-justified, then destroys them securely.

name: Mandatory Document Retention Duration Limitation
description: Provision requiring that documents be retained only for the duration that is legally required or business-justified. This establishes the upper bound on retention periods and prevents indefinite storage of documents.
context: FirstUK Bank retains documents only as long as legally required or business-justified

name: Secure Document Destruction Requirement
description: Provision mandating that documents must be destroyed securely once retention periods expire. This requirement ensures that sensitive information is not left vulnerable to unauthorized access or recovery after its business or legal purpose has ended.

name: Data Breach Risk
description: The risk that retained documents containing sensitive information may be accessed, disclosed, or recovered by unauthorized parties. This risk is mitigated through secure destruction practices once documents are no longer required.

name: Compliance Risk
description: The risk that FirstUK Bank may fail to meet legal retention requirements or retain documents beyond legally mandated periods, resulting in regulatory violations or enforcement action.
context: retains documents only as long as legally required

name: Secure Document Destruction Process
description: The operational safeguard requiring secure destruction of documents once retention periods expire. This control measure implements the policy's mandate to prevent unauthorized access to or recovery of sensitive information.

name: Data Retention Policy
description: A policy governing the retention and destruction of customer, account, and transaction documents across multiple document types. The policy specifies retention periods ranging from 2 to 6+ years post-closure or account tenure, with legal bases tied to POCA, AML regulations, and KYC requirements. Destruction methods include shredding and deletion.
context: Retention Period | Legal Basis | Destruction Method

name: Customer Profile Retention Requirement
description: Mandates retention of customer profile documents for the duration of account tenure plus 6 years, with legal basis in POCA, AML, and dispute resolution obligations.
context: Customer Profile | Account tenure + 6 years | POCA, AML, dispute | Shred/delete

name: KYC/CDD Records Retention Requirement
description: Mandates retention of Know Your Customer and Customer Due Diligence records for 5 years following account closure, with legal basis in the Money Laundering Regulations 2017.
context: KYC/CDD Records | 5 years post-closure | Money Laundering Regs 2017 | Shred/delete

name: Identification Document Retention Requirement
description: Mandates retention of identification documents for 6 years following account closure, with legal basis in POCA and anti-fraud obligations.
context: Identification Docs | 6 years post-closure | POCA, anti-fraud | Shred/delete

name: Address Verification Record Retention Requirement
description: Mandates retention of address verification records for 6 years following account closure, with legal basis in KYC requirements.
context: Address Verification | 6 years post-closure | KYC requirements | Shred/delete

name: Account Opening Form Retention Requirement
description: Mandates retention of account opening forms for 6 years following account closure, with legal basis in contract evidence requirements.
context: Account Opening Forms | 6 years post-closure | Contract evidence | Shred/delete

name: Statement Retention Requirement
description: Mandates retention of account statements for the duration of account tenure plus 6 years, with legal basis in customer service and dispute resolution obligations.
context: Statements | Account tenure + 6 years | Customer service, disputes | Shred/delete

name: Transaction Record Retention Requirement
description: Mandates retention of transaction records for a minimum of 6 years, with legal basis in POCA, audit, and dispute resolution obligations.
context: Transaction Records | 6 years minimum | POCA, audit, disputes | Shred/delete

name: Standing Order Record Retention Requirement
description: Mandates retention of standing order records for the duration of account tenure plus 2 years, with legal basis in contract evidence requirements.
context: Standing Orders | Account tenure + 2 years | Contract evidence | Delete

name: Direct Debit Mandate Retention Requirement
description: Mandates retention of direct debit mandates for 6 years following cancellation, with legal basis in Direct Debit scheme rules.
context: Direct Debit Mandates | 6 years post-cancellation | DD scheme rules | Shred/delete

name: Proceeds of Crime Act 2002
description: UK legislation establishing the legal basis for retention of customer profiles, identification documents, and transaction records as cited in this retention schedule.

name: Money Laundering Regulations 2017
description: UK regulation establishing the legal basis for retention of KYC and CDD records for 5 years post-closure.
context: KYC/CDD Records | 5 years post-closure | Money Laundering Regs 2017 | Shred/delete

name: Direct Debit Scheme Rules
description: Industry scheme rules establishing the legal basis for retention of direct debit mandates for 6 years post-cancellation.
context: Direct Debit Mandates | 6 years post-cancellation | DD scheme rules | Shred/delete

name: Money Laundering
description: Financial crime risk addressed through retention of customer profiles and transaction records as specified in the retention schedule.
context: Customer Profile | Account tenure + 6 years | POCA, AML, dispute

name: Fraud
description: Fraud risk addressed through retention of identification documents for 6 years post-closure.
context: Identification Docs | 6 years post-closure | POCA, anti-fraud | Shred/delete

name: Document Shredding
description: Physical destruction method for customer profiles, KYC/CDD records, identification documents, address verification records, account opening forms, statements, transaction records, and direct debit mandates upon expiry of retention periods.

name: Document Deletion
description: Digital destruction method for customer profiles, KYC/CDD records, identification documents, address verification records, account opening forms, statements, transaction records, and direct debit mandates upon expiry of retention periods.

name: Identification Document
description: Official identity documents required for KYC purposes and retained for 6 years post-closure under POCA and anti-fraud obligations.
context: Identification Docs | 6 years post-closure | POCA, anti-fraud | Shred/delete

name: Proof of Address
description: Address verification documents required for KYC purposes and retained for 6 years post-closure.
context: Address Verification | 6 years post-closure | KYC requirements | Shred/delete

name: Know Your Customer Verification
description: Customer identity and due diligence verification process with records retained for 5 years post-closure under Money Laundering Regulations 2017.
context: KYC/CDD Records | 5 years post-closure | Money Laundering Regs 2017 | Shred/delete
Address Verification | 6 years post-closure | KYC requirements | Shred/delete

name: Standing Order
description: Standing order payment instruction on customer accounts with records retained for account tenure plus 2 years as contract evidence.
context: Standing Orders | Account tenure + 2 years | Contract evidence | Delete

name: Direct Debit Mandate
description: Direct debit payment mandate on customer accounts with records retained for 6 years post-cancellation under Direct Debit scheme rules.
context: Direct Debit Mandates | 6 years post-cancellation | DD scheme rules | Shred/delete

name: Document Retention Policy
description: A policy governing the retention periods and legal bases for maintaining compliance and regulatory documents. The policy specifies distinct retention periods ranging from 3 to 7 years for various document types, with permanent retention for board and committee minutes. Legal basis is derived from FCA, PRA, and statutory audit requirements.
context: Compliance & Regulatory Documents | Document Type | Retention Period | Legal Basis
Complaint Files | 6 years from resolution | FCA COBS Part 2

name: Complaint File Retention Requirement
description: Complaint files must be retained for 6 years from the date of resolution. This requirement is mandated under FCA COBS Part 2 and ensures adequate documentation of complaint handling and resolution.
context: Complaint Files | 6 years from resolution | FCA COBS Part 2

name: Regulatory Report Retention Requirement
description: Regulatory reports must be retained for 5 years. This requirement is based on PRA Rulebook and audit obligations to maintain evidence of regulatory compliance and reporting.
context: Regulatory Reports | 5 years | PRA Rulebook, audit

name: AML Screening Results Retention Requirement
description: AML screening results must be retained for 5 years following account closure. This requirement is mandated under the Money Laundering Regulations to maintain audit trails of anti-money laundering compliance.
context: AML Screening Results | 5 years post-closure | Money Laundering Regs

name: SAR Filing Record Retention Requirement
description: Suspicious Activity Report records must be retained for 5 years. This requirement is mandated under the Proceeds of Crime Act to maintain documentation of suspicious activity reporting obligations.
context: SAR (Suspicious Activity) | 5 years | Proceeds of Crime Act

name: Audit Report Retention Requirement
description: Audit reports must be retained for 7 years. This requirement is based on statutory audit obligations to maintain evidence of internal and external audit activities.

name: Board and Committee Minutes Permanent Retention Requirement
description: Board and committee minutes must be retained permanently. This requirement is mandated under corporate governance principles to maintain a permanent record of governance decisions and deliberations.

name: Compliance Bulletin Retention Requirement
description: Compliance bulletins must be retained for 3 years. This requirement is based on regulatory reference obligations to maintain documentation of regulatory guidance and compliance communications.

name: Regulatory Circular Retention Requirement
description: Regulatory circulars must be retained for 3 to 5 years. This requirement is based on regulatory guidance obligations to maintain documentation of regulatory communications and directives.

name: Financial Conduct Authority COBS Part 2
description: FCA Conduct of Business sourcebook Part 2 establishes requirements for complaint handling and documentation. This regulation mandates the 6-year retention period for complaint files from resolution.
context: Complaint Files | 6 years from resolution | FCA COBS Part 2

name: PRA Rulebook
description: The PRA Rulebook establishes prudential requirements for regulated firms. It mandates the 5-year retention period for regulatory reports.
context: Regulatory Reports | 5 years | PRA Rulebook, audit

name: Money Laundering Regulations
description: The Money Laundering Regulations establish anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing obligations for financial institutions. They mandate the 5-year post-closure retention period for AML screening results.
context: AML Screening Results | 5 years post-closure | Money Laundering Regs

name: Proceeds of Crime Act
description: The Proceeds of Crime Act establishes the legal framework for reporting suspicious activity and money laundering. It mandates the 5-year retention period for Suspicious Activity Report records.
context: SAR (Suspicious Activity) | 5 years | Proceeds of Crime Act

name: Money Laundering
description: Money laundering risk is addressed through AML screening and SAR filing obligations, with records retained for 5 years post-closure to maintain audit trails and compliance evidence.
context: AML Screening Results | 5 years post-closure | Money Laundering Regs
SAR (Suspicious Activity) | 5 years | Proceeds of Crime Act

name: Regulatory Compliance Risk
description: Regulatory compliance risk is mitigated through retention of regulatory reports, audit reports, and compliance bulletins to maintain evidence of adherence to FCA, PRA, and statutory audit requirements.
context: Regulatory Reports | 5 years | PRA Rulebook, audit

name: AML Screening Results
description: AML screening results document the outcomes of anti-money laundering checks performed on customer accounts. Results must be retained for 5 years following account closure to maintain compliance evidence under the Money Laundering Regulations.
context: AML Screening Results | 5 years post-closure | Money Laundering Regs

name: Suspicious Activity Report Filing
description: Suspicious Activity Reports document and report suspicious transactions or activities to the relevant authority. SAR records must be retained for 5 years under the Proceeds of Crime Act.
context: SAR (Suspicious Activity) | 5 years | Proceeds of Crime Act

name: Document Retention Policy
description: A policy governing the retention periods and bases for operational, support, and compliance documents across the organisation. The policy establishes mandatory retention schedules for SOPs, policy documents, training records, disciplinary files, system logs, backups, and email communications, with retention periods ranging from 30 days to permanent, based on governance, legal, audit, and security requirements.
context: Operational & Support Documents | Document Type | Retention Period | Basis
Policy Documents | Permanent (all versions) | Governance, legal
Training Records | 3 years | Compliance training verification
System Access Logs | 1 year | Security, audit

name: Retention of Standard Operating Procedures and Procedures
description: Requires retention of current versions of SOPs and procedures plus the two prior versions to maintain governance and audit trail integrity.
context: SOPs & Procedures | Current + 2 prior versions | Governance, audit trail

name: Permanent Retention of Policy Documents
description: Mandates permanent retention of all versions of policy documents to satisfy governance and legal requirements.
context: Policy Documents | Permanent (all versions) | Governance, legal

name: Training Records Retention
description: Requires retention of training records for 3 years to enable verification of compliance training completion and audit compliance.
context: Training Records | 3 years | Compliance training verification

name: Staff Disciplinary Records Retention
description: Mandates retention of staff disciplinary records for 6 years from the date of action to comply with employment law requirements.
context: Staff Disciplinary | 6 years from action | Employment law

name: System Access Logs Retention
description: Requires retention of system access logs for 1 year to support security monitoring and audit requirements.
context: System Access Logs | 1 year | Security, audit

name: Backup Tapes Retention
description: Establishes a 30-day rotating retention schedule for backup tapes to support disaster recovery operations.

name: General Email Retention
description: Requires retention of general business email for 1–3 years to balance business efficiency with record-keeping obligations.

name: Legal and Compliance Email Retention
description: Mandates retention of email containing legal or compliance content for 7 years to satisfy legal hold and regulatory requirements.

name: Governance and Audit Trail Risk
description: The risk that inadequate retention of SOPs, procedures, and policy documents could compromise the organisation's ability to demonstrate governance compliance and maintain an auditable record of operational decisions.
context: SOPs & Procedures | Current + 2 prior versions | Governance, audit trail
Policy Documents | Permanent (all versions) | Governance, legal

name: Employment Law Compliance Risk
description: The risk of non-compliance with employment law arising from inadequate retention or loss of staff disciplinary records.
context: Staff Disciplinary | 6 years from action | Employment law

name: Security and Audit Risk
description: The risk that loss or inadequate retention of system access logs could compromise security monitoring capabilities and audit trail integrity.
context: System Access Logs | 1 year | Security, audit

name: Disaster Recovery Risk
description: The risk that inadequate backup tape retention could impair the organisation's ability to recover from system failures or data loss events.

name: Legal Hold and Regulatory Risk
description: The risk of non-compliance with legal hold obligations and regulatory requirements arising from inadequate retention of legal and compliance-related email communications.

name: Financial and Risk Document Retention Policy
description: Policy governing the retention periods for financial, risk, and compliance-related documents. Establishes mandatory retention schedules for general ledger, transaction ledger, risk assessments, incident reports, fraud investigations, and third-party vendor contracts based on accounting standards, regulatory requirements, and audit obligations.
context: Financial & Risk Documents | Document Type | Retention Period | Basis

name: General Ledger Record Retention Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to retain general ledger records for a period of 6 years, based on accounting standards compliance.

name: Transaction Ledger Record Retention Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to retain transaction ledger records for a period of 6 years, based on regulatory and audit requirements.

name: Risk Assessment Record Retention Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to retain risk assessment documentation for a period of 5 years, based on the bank's risk framework.

name: Incident Report Record Retention Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to retain incident reports for a period of 5 years to support loss data analysis and pattern identification.
context: Incident Reports | 5 years | Loss data, patterns

name: Fraud Investigation Record Retention Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to retain fraud investigation records for a period of 5 years to support fraud prevention efforts.

name: Third-Party Vendor Contract Record Retention Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to retain third-party vendor contracts for a period of 6 years following contract termination, based on contractual and compliance obligations.
context: Third-Party Vendor Contracts | 6 years post-termination | Contractual, compliance

name: Accounting Standards
description: Accounting standards that establish the basis for general ledger record retention requirements.

name: Regulatory and Audit Requirements
description: Regulatory and audit obligations that establish the basis for transaction ledger retention requirements.

name: Operational Risk
description: Operational risk addressed through retention of incident reports and loss data to identify patterns and support risk management.
context: Incident Reports | 5 years | Loss data, patterns

name: Fraud Risk
description: Fraud risk mitigated through retention of fraud investigation records to support fraud prevention initiatives.

name: Compliance Risk
description: Compliance risk managed through retention of third-party vendor contracts and financial records to meet contractual and regulatory obligations.
context: Third-Party Vendor Contracts | 6 years post-termination | Contractual, compliance

name: Data Retention Policy for Mortgage Documents
description: Policy governing the retention and lifecycle management of mortgage-related documents. Establishes extended retention periods for mortgage applications, underwriting files, property valuations, legal charges, and payment records due to the security interest (property lien) held by the bank.
context: Mortgages require extended retention due to security (property lien).

name: Mortgage Application Document Retention Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to retain mortgage application documents for the life of the loan plus 6 years following loan termination or payoff.
context: Mortgage Application | Life of loan + 6 years

name: Underwriting File Document Retention Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to retain underwriting files for the life of the loan plus 6 years following loan termination or payoff.
context: Underwriting File | Life of loan + 6 years

name: Property Valuation Document Retention Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to retain property valuation documents for the life of the loan plus 6 years following loan termination or payoff.
context: Property Valuation | Life of loan + 6 years

name: Legal Charge and Deed Document Retention Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to retain legal charge documents and deeds for the life of the loan plus 6 years following loan termination or payoff, reflecting the bank's security interest in the property.
context: Legal Charge/Deed | Life of loan + 6 years

name: Mortgage Payment Records Retention Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to retain payment records for the life of the loan plus 6 years following loan termination or payoff.
context: Payment Records | Life of loan + 6 years

name: Property Lien Security Risk
description: The operational and legal risk arising from the bank's security interest (property lien) in mortgaged properties, necessitating extended document retention to evidence and protect the bank's claim.
context: Mortgages require extended retention due to security (property lien).

name: Mortgage Product
description: Secured lending product where the bank holds a legal charge over residential or commercial property as security. Subject to extended document retention requirements due to the nature of the security interest.
context: Mortgages require extended retention due to security (property lien).

name: Data Retention Policy
description: Policy governing the extended retention of customer records and documents beyond standard retention periods. Specifies conditions triggering extended holds, including active disputes, regulatory investigations, legal proceedings, and explicit customer requests, with annual reassessment requirements.
context: Retention Extended If: Customer dispute is active (until resolution + 6 years)

name: Extended Retention During Active Customer Dispute
description: Mandatory requirement to retain all customer records and documents for the duration of an active customer dispute plus an additional 6 years following resolution.
context: Customer dispute is active (until resolution + 6 years)

name: Extended Retention During Regulatory Investigation
description: Mandatory requirement to retain all customer records and documents for the duration of any ongoing regulatory investigation.

name: Extended Retention During Legal Proceedings
description: Mandatory requirement to retain all customer records and documents for the duration of pending legal action plus an additional 6 years following conclusion.

name: Retention Upon Customer Request
description: Mandatory requirement to retain customer records when explicitly requested by the customer, with documentation of the request required.

name: Retention Compliance with Regulatory Requirements
description: Mandatory requirement to retain customer records in compliance with all applicable regulatory requirements including GDPR and POCA.

name: Legal Hold Documentation and Marking
description: Mandatory requirement to place documents on legal hold and mark them 'Do Not Destroy' when retention is extended.

name: Annual Reassessment of Legal Holds
description: Mandatory requirement to reassess all legal holds on an annual basis to determine whether retention conditions remain applicable.

name: Destruction Upon Legal Hold Lift
description: Mandatory requirement to destroy retained documents once the legal hold has been lifted and retention conditions no longer apply.

name: General Data Protection Regulation
description: EU regulation governing data protection and privacy, referenced as a regulatory requirement that may trigger extended retention obligations.

name: Proceeds of Crime Act
description: UK legislation governing anti-money laundering and asset recovery, referenced as a regulatory requirement that may trigger extended retention obligations.

name: Regulatory Investigation Risk
description: Risk of regulatory investigation into customer accounts or transactions, which triggers extended document retention requirements.

name: Legal Dispute Risk
description: Risk of customer disputes or legal proceedings requiring preservation of evidence and extended document retention.
context: Customer dispute is active (until resolution + 6 years)

name: Legal Hold Marking and Documentation
description: Operational control requiring documents subject to extended retention to be placed on legal hold and marked 'Do Not Destroy' to prevent inadvertent destruction.

name: Annual Legal Hold Reassessment
description: Operational control requiring annual review and reassessment of all active legal holds to determine whether retention conditions remain applicable.

name: Document Retention and Early Destruction Policy
description: Policy governing the early destruction of documents across multiple categories including emails, system logs, and compliance records. Establishes retention periods based on document type and compliance status, with mandatory legal hold confirmation and secure destruction procedures.

name: Routine Operational Email Retention
description: Routine operational emails must be retained for a minimum of 1 year before destruction is permitted.

name: Compliance Email Retention with Legal Hold
description: Compliance-related emails must be retained for 7 years and placed under legal hold status, preventing early destruction.

name: External Email Archive Retention
description: Emails archived to external storage must be retained for 3 years before destruction eligibility.

name: General Transaction Log Retention
description: General transaction system logs must be retained for a minimum of 1 year before destruction.

name: System Log Backup Retention
description: System logs archived for backup purposes must be retained for 30 days minimum.

name: Compliance and Audit Log Retention
description: Compliance and audit logs must be retained for a minimum of 1 year before destruction is permitted.

name: Legal Hold Confirmation Before Destruction
description: Before scheduling any document for destruction, confirmation must be obtained that no legal hold applies to the document.

name: Secure Document Destruction Execution
description: All documents scheduled for destruction must be destroyed using secure methods to prevent unauthorized recovery or access.

name: Destruction Confirmation and Documentation
description: After destruction is completed, confirmation of destruction must be obtained and documented for audit and compliance purposes.

name: Document Categorization Process
description: Operational control requiring documents to be categorized by type (email, system logs, etc.) as the first step in the destruction workflow.

name: Legal Hold Verification Control
description: Control mechanism to verify and confirm that no legal hold applies to a document before it is scheduled for destruction.

name: Destruction Scheduling System
description: Operational control for scheduling documents for destruction based on retention period expiration and legal hold clearance.

name: Secure Destruction Method
description: Technical and operational safeguard ensuring documents are destroyed securely to prevent unauthorized recovery or access to sensitive information.

name: Destruction Audit Trail
description: Control requiring confirmation and documentation of all document destruction events for audit, compliance, and accountability purposes.

name: Document Destruction Policy
description: Policy governing the destruction of physical documents through approved methods including on-site shredding and professional third-party destruction services. Establishes requirements for destruction logs, certificates of destruction, and chain of custody maintenance.

name: On-Site Document Shredding Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to use on-site shredder for document destruction when volume is less than 10 pages per day, with documents shredded before recycling and a destruction log maintained.

name: Professional Third-Party Destruction Service Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to engage a third-party secure destruction company for document destruction, with certificate of destruction provided, scheduled pickup on monthly or quarterly basis, and chain of custody maintained throughout the process.

name: Document Destruction Log
description: Record-keeping control measure requiring documentation of all document destruction activities, particularly for on-site shredding operations.

name: Certificate of Destruction
description: Record-keeping control measure requiring third-party destruction companies to provide certificates of destruction as evidence of secure document disposal.

name: Chain of Custody Maintenance
description: Audit and accountability control measure requiring maintenance of chain of custody documentation for documents transferred to third-party destruction services.

name: On-Site Document Shredder
description: Physical safeguard control measure using on-site shredding equipment for destruction of documents when daily volume is less than 10 pages.

name: Digital Records Management Policy
description: Policy governing the secure deletion and destruction of digital records, including data overwriting, encrypted deletion, and physical destruction procedures. Establishes a five-step process for identifying, quarantining, securely deleting, verifying, and certifying the destruction of files.
context: Secure Deletion: Data overwriting (DoD standard, 3-pass), Encrypted deletion (AES-256), Physical destruction (hard drives)
Process: 1. Identify files to destroy 2. Quarantine to destruction folder 3. Secure delete (not just recycle bin) 4. Verify deletion 5. Certificate generated

name: Data Overwriting Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to overwrite data using the DoD standard 3-pass method as part of secure deletion procedures for digital records.

name: Encrypted Deletion Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to perform encrypted deletion using AES-256 encryption standard as part of secure deletion procedures for digital records.

name: Physical Destruction Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to physically destroy hard drives and other storage media containing sensitive data as part of the secure deletion process.

name: File Identification and Quarantine
description: Mandatory requirement to identify files designated for destruction and quarantine them to a dedicated destruction folder prior to secure deletion.
context: 1. Identify files to destroy 2. Quarantine to destruction folder

name: Secure Deletion Execution
description: Mandatory requirement to perform secure deletion of quarantined files using approved methods, ensuring data is not recoverable through standard recycle bin recovery.

name: Deletion Verification
description: Mandatory requirement to verify that deletion has been completed successfully and data is no longer accessible.

name: Destruction Certificate Generation
description: Mandatory requirement to generate and maintain a certificate documenting the completion of the secure deletion and destruction process.

name: Data Overwriting Control
description: Operational control implementing the DoD standard 3-pass data overwriting method to ensure secure deletion of digital records.

name: AES-256 Encrypted Deletion
description: Operational control implementing AES-256 encryption standard for secure deletion of digital records.

name: Physical Media Destruction
description: Operational control for the physical destruction of hard drives and storage media containing sensitive data.

name: Destruction Folder Quarantine
description: Operational control establishing a dedicated quarantine folder to isolate files designated for destruction prior to secure deletion.

name: Deletion Verification Process
description: Operational control to verify successful completion of secure deletion and confirm data is no longer accessible.

name: Destruction Certificate Documentation
description: Operational control requiring generation and maintenance of certificates documenting completion of secure deletion and destruction processes.

name: Records Management Policy
description: Policy governing the digital retention, tracking, and destruction of records within the bank's document management system. Establishes requirements for retention date tracking, automated alerts, destruction logging, and audit trail maintenance.
context: Document storage system (DMS-001) tracks retention dates

name: Retention Date Tracking Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement that the document management system must track and record retention dates for all stored documents to ensure compliance with retention schedules.
context: Document storage system (DMS-001) tracks retention dates

name: Pre-Destruction Alert Notification
description: Requirement to generate automated alerts 30 days prior to scheduled document destruction, providing advance notice for review and approval before deletion.

name: Destruction Event Logging
description: Mandatory requirement to maintain a comprehensive destruction log that records all document deletions, including dates, document identifiers, and destruction authorization details.

name: Audit Trail Maintenance
description: Requirement to maintain a complete audit trail of all records management activities, including document storage, retention tracking, alerts, and destruction events for compliance verification and investigation purposes.

name: Document Management System
description: Digital system (DMS-001) that implements records management controls through automated retention date tracking, pre-destruction alerts, destruction logging, and audit trail functionality.
context: Document storage system (DMS-001) tracks retention dates

name: Automated Pre-Destruction Alert System
description: Automated notification mechanism that triggers 30 days before scheduled document destruction, serving as a control gate to prevent premature or unauthorized deletion.

name: Destruction Log
description: Permanent record-keeping mechanism that documents all document destruction events, providing evidence of compliance with retention schedules and supporting audit and investigation activities.

name: Data Deletion and Right to Erasure Policy
description: Policy governing customer requests for data deletion under GDPR Right to Erasure. FirstUK Bank may refuse deletion where legal obligations exist, particularly under POCA and AML regulations. The policy establishes a four-step assessment and notification procedure.
context: FirstUK Bank may refuse if legal obligation exists
Exception: POCA, AML records (cannot delete if regulatory required)
If no hold: Destroy and confirm

name: Customer Right to Request Data Deletion
description: Customers have the right to request deletion of their personal data under GDPR. This provision establishes the customer's entitlement to initiate the erasure process.

name: Bank Right to Refuse Deletion on Legal Grounds
description: FirstUK Bank may refuse customer deletion requests where legal obligations require data retention. This provision protects the bank's compliance obligations under financial crime and regulatory frameworks.
context: FirstUK Bank may refuse if legal obligation exists
Exception: POCA, AML records (cannot delete if regulatory required)

name: Legal Hold Assessment Process
description: Upon receipt of a deletion request, FirstUK Bank must assess whether legal holds apply to the customer's data. The assessment determines whether deletion can proceed or must be refused.
context: If no hold: Destroy and confirm
If hold: Explain reason and timeframe

name: Deletion Request Notification and Confirmation
description: FirstUK Bank must confirm deletion to the customer when no legal hold exists, or explain the reason and timeframe for retention when a hold is in place.
context: If no hold: Destroy and confirm
If hold: Explain reason and timeframe

name: General Data Protection Regulation
description: EU/UK data protection regulation establishing the Right to Erasure (Right to be Forgotten) that forms the legal basis for this policy. GDPR permits data controllers to refuse erasure where legal obligations require retention.
context: GDPR Right to Erasure ("Right to be Forgotten")
Exception: POCA, AML records (cannot delete if regulatory required)

name: Proceeds of Crime Act
description: UK legislation establishing financial crime investigation and asset recovery obligations. POCA creates a legal hold exception preventing deletion of customer records where required for proceeds of crime investigations.
context: Exception: POCA, AML records (cannot delete if regulatory required)

name: Anti-Money Laundering Regulations
description: Regulatory framework requiring financial institutions to maintain records for AML compliance purposes. AML obligations create a legal hold exception preventing deletion of customer data where regulatory record retention is mandated.
context: Exception: POCA, AML records (cannot delete if regulatory required)

name: Regulatory Non-Compliance Risk
description: Risk that premature deletion of customer data could breach POCA or AML record retention obligations, exposing FirstUK Bank to regulatory sanctions and enforcement action.
context: Exception: POCA, AML records (cannot delete if regulatory required)
If hold: Explain reason and timeframe

name: Legal Hold Assessment Control
description: Operational control requiring FirstUK Bank to assess and document legal holds before processing any customer deletion request. This gate prevents inadvertent deletion of data subject to regulatory retention obligations.
context: If no hold: Destroy and confirm
If hold: Explain reason and timeframe

name: Data Destruction and Confirmation Process
description: Operational procedure requiring FirstUK Bank to destroy customer data when no legal hold exists and to provide written confirmation of destruction to the customer.
context: If no hold: Destroy and confirm

name: Customer
description: Natural person holding a banking relationship with FirstUK Bank who may exercise the right to request deletion of their personal data under GDPR.

name: FirstUK Bank
description: The data controller responsible for assessing deletion requests, determining legal holds, and either destroying data or explaining retention reasons to customers.
context: FirstUK Bank may refuse if legal obligation exists
If no hold: Destroy and confirm

name: Dispute and Legal Holds Policy
description: Policy governing the retention and destruction of documents during customer disputes, legal actions, and regulatory investigations. Establishes mandatory hold procedures, marking requirements, and destruction timelines based on dispute resolution or regulator instruction.
context: Litigation Hold: Customer dispute or legal action

name: Litigation Hold on Customer Dispute
description: Mandatory requirement to retain all relevant documents when a customer dispute or legal action is initiated. Documents must be marked as 'Legal Hold' and cannot be destroyed during the dispute period.

name: Document Destruction Timeline After Dispute Resolution
description: Specifies that documents subject to litigation hold must be retained for 6 years following the resolution of a customer dispute or legal action before destruction is permitted.

name: Regulatory Investigation Document Hold
description: Mandatory requirement to retain all documents specified by a regulator when a regulatory investigation is initiated. The bank must follow the regulator's timeline and destroy documents only per regulator instruction.

name: Legal and Compliance Risk
description: Risk of non-compliance with legal obligations and regulatory requirements arising from improper document retention or destruction during disputes and investigations. Encompasses litigation exposure and regulatory sanction risk.

name: Legal Hold Document Marking
description: Operational control requiring documents subject to litigation hold to be explicitly marked as 'Legal Hold' to ensure they are not inadvertently destroyed and to maintain clear audit trail of hold status.

name: Regulator-Directed Document Retention
description: Control measure requiring the bank to retain all documents specified by a regulator during an investigation and to follow the regulator's timeline for destruction, ensuring compliance with regulatory directives.

name: Regulator
description: External regulatory authority with the power to request document holds during investigations and to direct the timeline and manner of document destruction. The bank must comply with all regulator instructions regarding document retention.

name: Customer in Dispute
description: A customer engaged in a dispute or legal action with the bank, triggering mandatory document retention obligations and litigation hold procedures.

name: Records Audit Policy
description: Policy governing the annual audit of record retention practices, including sample file review, destruction logs, and compliance assessment with the retention schedule. Includes evaluation of unauthorized destruction incidents.

name: Regulatory Audit Policy
description: Policy establishing regulatory audit obligations including FCA/PRA periodic reviews, document retention sampling, and POCA compliance assessment.

name: Annual Audit of Retention Practices
description: Mandatory annual audit requirement to review and assess the bank's record retention practices and compliance with established retention schedules.

name: Sample File Review and Destruction Log Assessment
description: Requirement to conduct sample file reviews and examine destruction logs as part of audit procedures to verify proper record handling and disposal.

name: Unauthorized Destruction Assessment
description: Audit obligation to assess and identify any instances of unauthorized destruction of records outside approved retention schedules.

name: FCA and PRA Periodic Review Compliance
description: Requirement to comply with periodic regulatory reviews conducted by the FCA and PRA regarding document retention and compliance practices.

name: Document Retention Sampling for Regulatory Review
description: Obligation to provide document retention samples to regulatory authorities during periodic reviews to demonstrate compliance with retention requirements.

name: POCA Compliance Assessment
description: Requirement to assess and demonstrate compliance with Proceeds of Crime Act (POCA) obligations during regulatory audits.

name: Financial Conduct Authority
description: UK financial regulator conducting periodic reviews of document retention and compliance practices as referenced in the audit policy.

name: Prudential Regulation Authority
description: UK prudential regulator conducting periodic reviews of document retention and compliance practices as referenced in the audit policy.

name: Proceeds of Crime Act
description: UK legislation governing anti-money laundering and proceeds of crime compliance, subject to audit assessment as part of regulatory compliance obligations.

name: Destruction Log Review
description: Control mechanism involving sample review of destruction logs to verify proper documentation and authorization of record disposal activities.

name: Retention Schedule Compliance Verification
description: Control procedure to verify that record retention and destruction practices comply with the established retention schedule through periodic audit.

name: Document Retention and Destruction Policy
description: A policy governing staff responsibilities for document management, including retention periods, destruction schedules, legal holds, and customer requests. The policy establishes obligations for document owners to maintain compliance with retention requirements and handle customer data requests appropriately.

name: Knowledge of Document Retention Period
description: Document owners must be aware of and understand the applicable retention period for documents under their control.

name: Compliance with Destruction Schedule
description: Document owners must comply with the established destruction schedule for documents that have reached the end of their retention period.

name: Legal Hold Flagging
description: Document owners must identify and flag documents subject to legal holds to prevent their destruction and ensure preservation for legal proceedings.

name: Customer Request Documentation
description: Document owners must record and document all customer requests related to their documents, ensuring proper tracking and response.

name: Document Owner
description: A staff role responsible for managing documents under their control, including maintaining knowledge of retention periods, ensuring compliance with destruction schedules, flagging legal holds, and documenting customer requests.

name: Records Management Policy
description: A policy governing the retention, destruction, monitoring, and audit of records in compliance with regulatory and operational requirements. The policy establishes obligations for maintaining retention schedules, monitoring destruction activities, verifying compliance, and conducting records management audits.

name: Retention Schedule Maintenance
description: A mandatory requirement to maintain and keep current a retention schedule that governs how long records must be kept before destruction.

name: Destruction Monitoring
description: A mandatory requirement to actively monitor the destruction of records to ensure it is carried out in accordance with the retention schedule and applicable policies.

name: Compliance Verification
description: A mandatory requirement to verify that records management activities comply with established policies, retention schedules, and regulatory obligations.

name: Records Management Audit
description: A mandatory requirement to conduct periodic audits of records management practices to assess adherence to retention schedules, destruction procedures, and compliance obligations.

name: Retention Schedule
description: A documented control mechanism that specifies retention periods for different categories of records, enabling consistent application of retention rules and supporting compliance verification.

name: Destruction Monitoring Process
description: An operational safeguard that tracks and documents the destruction of records to ensure it occurs only when authorized and in compliance with retention schedules.

name: Records Management Audit Process
description: A periodic review mechanism designed to assess the effectiveness of records retention, destruction, and compliance verification activities across the organization.

name: Training and Awareness Policy
description: A mandatory annual training policy requiring all staff, managers, and compliance personnel to complete document retention awareness and governance training at specified intervals and durations.
context: All staff: Document retention awareness (30 min)

name: Document Retention Awareness Training for All Staff
description: Mandatory requirement for all staff to complete a 30-minute document retention awareness training session annually.
context: All staff: Document retention awareness (30 min)

name: Retention Responsibility Training for Managers
description: Mandatory requirement for managers to complete a 60-minute training session on retention responsibility annually.

name: Advanced Retention Governance Training for Compliance
description: Mandatory requirement for compliance personnel to complete a 2-hour advanced retention governance training session annually.

name: All Staff
description: All staff members are responsible for completing mandatory annual document retention awareness training of 30 minutes.
context: All staff: Document retention awareness (30 min)

name: Managers
description: Managers are responsible for completing mandatory annual training on retention responsibility lasting 60 minutes.

name: Compliance Personnel
description: Compliance personnel are responsible for completing mandatory annual advanced retention governance training lasting 2 hours.

name: Staff Training Program
description: A mandatory annual training control measure covering document retention awareness for all staff, retention responsibility for managers, and advanced retention governance for compliance personnel.
context: All staff: Document retention awareness (30 min)

name: Policy Review and Update Framework
description: A governance framework establishing the schedule and triggers for reviewing and updating banking policies. The policy mandates annual reviews or reviews upon regulatory change, with documented review dates and next review scheduling.
context: Review Frequency: Annual (or upon regulatory change)

name: Annual Policy Review Requirement
description: A mandatory requirement that all policies must be reviewed on an annual basis, or triggered earlier upon any regulatory change. This provision ensures policies remain current and compliant with evolving regulatory requirements.
context: Review Frequency: Annual (or upon regulatory change)

name: Regulatory Change Triggered Policy Review
description: A mandatory requirement that policies must be reviewed and updated immediately upon any regulatory change, in addition to the standard annual review cycle. This ensures the bank maintains compliance with new or amended regulatory obligations.
context: Review Frequency: Annual (or upon regulatory change)

name: Policy Review Documentation and Scheduling
description: A requirement to document and maintain records of policy review dates, including the date of the last review and the scheduled date for the next review. This provision ensures audit trail and accountability for policy governance.

name: Privacy Policy
description: A policy governing GDPR data retention obligations and practices. Referenced as a related document in the context of data management and destruction procedures.

name: General Data Protection Regulation
description: EU regulation establishing data protection and privacy requirements, including data retention obligations referenced in the privacy policy.

name: Document Management System
description: A system for managing documents within the organization, referenced as DMS-001 in the document management framework.

name: Destruction Certificate
description: A template document used to evidence and record the destruction of records in compliance with data retention and disposal policies.

name: Head of Compliance
description: Senior role responsible for compliance oversight and policy approval. Holds authority to sign off on policy documents and ensure regulatory adherence across the organization.
context: Approved by: Head of Compliance — Date: 2026-01-15

name: Data Protection Officer
description: Designated role with responsibility for data protection compliance and policy approval. Required to sign off on policies affecting data handling and privacy obligations.

name: General Counsel
description: Senior legal role responsible for legal review and approval of policy documents. Provides legal authority and oversight for policy compliance and regulatory alignment.
